The existence of the curve in the calculation is evidence that a unitary resolution is compatible with semi-classical gravity. The microscopic realisation remains open.

title: The Island Formula
paras: The island formula computes the entanglement entropy of the radiation as the minimum of the generalised entropy of a region that includes an island inside the black hole. The formula is \[ S = \min \left( \frac{\mathrm{Area}(\partial I)}{4G_N} + S_{\mathrm{matter}}(R \cup I) \right). \] The minimum is taken over islands \( I \). After the Page time the minimum includes a non-empty island. The formula reproduces the Page curve.

It has been derived from the replica trick in gravitational path integrals. It applies to evaporating black holes in anti-de Sitter space and in certain flat-space models. Its validity for realistic astrophysical black holes is assumed but not proven. The formula is the sharpest present statement of how information escapes. It remains a semi-classical expression.

title: Quantum Biology
paras: Most biological processes are well described by classical chemistry. A few involve quantum effects that cannot be ignored.

Enzyme catalysis sometimes uses tunneling. In hydrogen-transfer reactions the proton or hydrogen atom can pass through the energy barrier rather than over it. The rate is higher than a classical calculation predicts. Kinetic isotope effects—the change in rate when hydrogen is replaced by deuterium—are larger than expected from mass alone and are consistent with tunneling. The effect is temperature-dependent in ways that match quantum models.

Photosynthetic light-harvesting complexes transfer energy from antenna pigments to the reaction center with high efficiency. Spectroscopic measurements show coherent oscillations in the energy transfer. The coherence persists for hundreds of femtoseconds at physiological temperatures. Whether the coherence improves the efficiency under natural conditions or is a side effect of the structure is still under study. The observation is established. The functional importance is not fully settled.

Avian magnetoreception is another candidate. Some migratory birds orient using the Earth’s magnetic field. One proposed mechanism is a radical-pair reaction in cryptochrome proteins in the eye. The yield of the reaction depends on the orientation of the radical pair relative to the magnetic field because of the interplay of electron spins. The mechanism is plausible and consistent with behavioral experiments. Direct proof that it is the sensor used by the bird is still incomplete.

Quantum effects in biology are real where they have been measured. They do not require that the organism maintain macroscopic coherence. They occur in specific reactions where the energy barriers, the timescales, and the isolation from the environment allow them. The majority of cellular chemistry remains classical. The exceptions show that evolution can use quantum mechanics when it is available.

title: No-Cloning and Quantum Information
paras: An unknown quantum state cannot be copied. Suppose a machine takes a system in an arbitrary state and produces two systems in that same state, while leaving the original unchanged. The linearity of quantum mechanics forbids it. If the machine works for two orthogonal states, it fails for their superposition. The proof is short. It is called the no-cloning theorem.

The theorem has practical consequences. It prevents the use of quantum states as ordinary classical bits that can be duplicated and checked. It is the reason quantum key distribution can detect eavesdropping. Any attempt to measure or copy the quantum signals disturbs them in a way that the legitimate parties can observe. It also limits what a quantum computer can do with an unknown state. The state can be teleported if the original is destroyed, but it cannot be cloned.

Quantum information is carried by qubits. A qubit can be in a superposition of two states. Two qubits can be entangled. The joint state cannot be written as a product of individual states. Measurement of one qubit instantly correlates with the measurement of the other, regardless of distance. The correlation does not allow faster-than-light signaling. The outcomes are random. Only when the results are compared does the correlation appear. Entanglement is a resource for computation and for communication. It is also the feature that makes the measurement problem sharp. The linear evolution produces superpositions. The observed world contains definite outcomes. How the transition occurs is not settled by the formalism.

The no-cloning theorem, entanglement, and the limits on signaling are established. They follow from the linearity and the tensor-product structure of quantum mechanics. They constrain every interpretation and every proposed application.

title: Bell’s Theorem and the Experiments
paras: In 1935 Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen argued that quantum mechanics is incomplete. They considered two particles that have interacted and then separated. A measurement on one instantly determines the result of a corresponding measurement on the other. If the particles have definite properties all along, the correlation is ordinary. If they do not, the theory appears to require a nonlocal influence. Einstein called the second possibility spooky.

John Bell showed in 1964 that the two pictures are not equivalent. Any theory in which the outcomes are determined by local hidden variables must satisfy a certain inequality on the correlations. Quantum mechanics violates the inequality for some choices of measurements. The violation is a quantitative prediction. It can be tested.

Experiments beginning in the 1970s and culminating in the work of Aspect, Dalibard, and Roger in 1982 measured the correlations with polarizers whose settings were changed while the particles were in flight. The results matched the quantum prediction and violated the Bell inequality. Later experiments closed the main loopholes: the detection loophole, the locality loophole, and the freedom-of-choice loophole. The violation is established.

The experiments rule out local hidden-variable theories. They do not by themselves select among the remaining interpretations. The correlations are real. They do not allow signaling. The random outcomes on each side remain random. Only the joint statistics show the violation. Quantum teleportation uses the same resource. An unknown state can be transferred from one system to another by a joint measurement and classical communication. The original state is destroyed. No information travels faster than light. The protocol has been demonstrated with photons and with atoms.

The theorem and the experiments fix one boundary. Any complete account of the correlations must abandon either locality or the assumption that the outcomes are determined by preexisting local variables, or both. The boundary is experimental.

title: The Precision of Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Quantum electrodynamics is the theory of electrons, positrons, and photons. It is the most precisely tested theory in physics. The magnetic moment of the electron is predicted and measured to more than ten significant figures. The agreement holds.

The Dirac equation gives the electron a g-factor of exactly 2. Quantum corrections change it. The leading correction, calculated by Schwinger in 1948, is \( a = (g-2)/2 = \alpha/(2\pi) \), where \( \alpha \) is the fine-structure constant. Higher-order terms in powers of \( \alpha \) have been calculated. The experimental value of the anomaly is \( a_e = 0.00115965218059(13) \). The theoretical value, limited by the precision of \( \alpha \) itself, matches within the uncertainties.

The Lamb shift is the splitting between the \( 2s_{1/2} \) and \( 2p_{1/2} \) levels of hydrogen. In the Dirac theory they are degenerate. The measured interval is about 1057 MHz. The dominant contribution comes from the electron’s interaction with the fluctuating electromagnetic field. A smaller contribution, about −27 MHz, comes from vacuum polarization, the Uehling effect. The full calculation, including higher orders, matches the measurement.

The fine-structure constant is not constant. It runs with the energy scale. Vacuum polarization screens the charge at long distances. At shorter distances the effective charge is larger. The running is logarithmic. At the mass of the Z boson, \( 1/\alpha \) is about 128.9 rather than 137.0. The running is measured in scattering experiments and is consistent with the calculation.

Renormalization is the procedure that makes these predictions finite. Loop diagrams produce divergent integrals. The divergences are absorbed into the definitions of the measured mass and charge. Once those quantities are fixed by experiment, the remaining predictions are finite and unambiguous. The procedure is not an arbitrary subtraction. It is required by the structure of the theory and is constrained by gauge invariance. The Ward identity ensures that the renormalization of the vertex and of the electron field are related, so that the charge remains universal.

The precision is possible because the expansion parameter \( \alpha \) is small. Each additional loop is suppressed by another factor of \( \alpha/\pi \). The same methods applied to the strong force do not converge in the same way at low energy. QED is both a working computational tool and a demonstration that a quantum field theory can be defined, renormalized, and tested to extraordinary accuracy. Its success fixes the standard against which other theories are judged.

title: Feynman’s Account of Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Richard Feynman presented quantum electrodynamics in a form that begins with amplitudes rather than with fields. Every photon carries a complex amplitude, which can be drawn as an arrow. The arrow has a length and a direction. The probability that an event occurs is the square of the length of the final arrow. When an event can happen in more than one way, the arrows for the different ways are added before the square is taken. Interference is the result of that addition. Nature, it seems, prefers to do the arithmetic first and the squaring later, which is the opposite of the order most of us learned in school and have been regretting ever since.

Light is partially reflected from a surface of glass. The probability depends on the thickness of the glass. The calculation sums the amplitudes for reflection from the front surface and from the back surface. The relative phase depends on the extra distance traveled. The same rule accounts for the reflection from a mirror, the focusing of a lens, and the diffraction by a grating. In each case every possible path contributes an amplitude. Paths near the classical path have nearly the same phase and add constructively. Paths far from the classical path cancel.

An electron also carries an amplitude for going from one point to another. The amplitude depends on the proper time along the path. An electron can emit or absorb a photon. Those three processes—the photon going from place to place, the electron going from place to place, and the electron emitting or absorbing a photon—are the only ingredients. Every electromagnetic process is a combination of them. The combinations are drawn as diagrams. Each diagram corresponds to a term in the calculation. The terms are added, and the square of the sum is the probability.

The theory is approximate. Higher-order diagrams contain loops and produce large intermediate numbers. Those numbers are absorbed into the measured mass and charge of the electron. Once that is done, the remaining predictions are finite. The magnetic moment of the electron, the Lamb shift, and the scattering of light by light are calculated and measured to high precision. The agreement is the strongest quantitative success in physics.

The account does not eliminate the mathematics. It shows what the mathematics is doing. Amplitudes are added for every way an event can happen. The classical path is the path that survives the addition. The photon is the quantum of the electromagnetic field. The same rules govern the emission of light by an atom, the reflection of light by a mirror, and the forces between charges. The strangeness is not removed. It is located in the rule that the arrows must be added before they are squared.

title: The Technical Structure of Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Feynman’s formulation of quantum electrodynamics supplies a set of rules for calculating any electromagnetic process. The amplitude for a particle to go from one point to another is given by a propagator. For the electron the propagator is the Green function of the Dirac equation. For the photon it is the Green function of the wave equation. Both are known in closed form.

An interaction occurs when an electron emits or absorbs a photon. The vertex contributes a factor proportional to the charge and to the Dirac matrix \(\gamma^\mu\). Momentum is conserved at every vertex. The full amplitude for a process is the sum of the amplitudes for every diagram that connects the initial state to the final state. Each internal line is a propagator. Each closed loop is integrated over the momentum that circulates in it.

The path-integral version of the same theory states that the amplitude is the sum over all field histories of \(e^{iS/\hbar}\), where \(S\) is the classical action. The Feynman rules are the perturbative expansion of that sum. The two formulations are equivalent. The diagrams are a bookkeeping device for the expansion. They are not pictures of trajectories.

Ultraviolet divergences appear in the loop integrals. They are handled by renormalization. The bare mass and charge in the Lagrangian are not the measured mass and charge. The difference absorbs the divergent parts. After renormalization every physical prediction is finite. Infrared divergences appear when massless photons are emitted with vanishing energy. They cancel in any observable that sums over all soft photons that cannot be resolved. The cancellation is required by the structure of the theory.

The same rules give the anomalous magnetic moment, the Lamb shift, the running of the charge, and the cross sections for scattering and pair production. Each additional loop is suppressed by a power of the fine-structure constant. The expansion is therefore practical. The theory remains the prototype of a renormalizable quantum field theory. Its rules are specific to electrons and photons. The same diagrammatic method, with different vertices and propagators, is used for the other forces.

title: Quantum Effects in Genetics
paras: Most genetic processes are classical. Base pairing, replication, transcription, and translation are described by ordinary chemistry. A few steps show quantum signatures that affect the outcome.

Proton tunneling contributes to some mutation rates. In DNA the hydrogen bonds that hold base pairs together can shift by tunneling. The tautomeric forms that result can mispair during replication. The rate is low. It is not zero. The contribution is measurable in some systems by comparing rates in ordinary water and in heavy water. The difference is consistent with a tunneling component. The bulk of mutations still arise from other causes: copying errors, chemical damage, and radiation. Tunneling is one channel among several.

Electron transfer in some repair enzymes and in photosynthetic reaction centers proceeds by tunneling. The distance dependence and the temperature dependence match quantum calculations. The proteins position the donors and acceptors so that the tunneling rate is useful. The positioning is the product of selection. The tunneling itself is a physical fact that selection has used.

No evidence currently supports the claim that genetic information is stored or processed in a macroscopic quantum superposition inside the cell. Decoherence times at biological temperatures and in the wet environment of the nucleus are extremely short. The successful descriptions of heredity, development, and evolution remain classical. The quantum contributions that have been demonstrated are local, specific, and already incorporated into the ordinary chemical account. They do not require a separate quantum genetics. They show that the chemistry of life includes the quantum mechanics of its atoms.

title: Adaptive Mutation and Quantum Coherence
paras: In 1999 Johnjoe McFadden and Jim Al-Khalili proposed a quantum model for adaptive mutation. Adaptive mutation is the reported phenomenon in which certain mutations appear more frequently when they confer an advantage than when they are neutral. The classical expectation is that mutation rates are independent of utility. The observations, first described in bacteria under starvation, have been disputed. Some are explained by ordinary growth and selection on pre-existing variants. Others remain unresolved.

The quantum proposal begins with proton tunneling in DNA base pairs. A proton can occupy either of two positions. The two positions correspond to different base-pairing possibilities. The model treats the proton as remaining in a coherent superposition of the two positions for a biologically relevant time. Interaction with an environment that contains a usable substrate is argued to accelerate decoherence and thereby increase the rate at which the mutant state is realized. The estimated decoherence time in the model is on the order of seconds. That is long enough, in principle, for the proposed effect.

The proposal has not been confirmed. Direct measurements of coherence in DNA under cellular conditions have not shown the required superposition. Decoherence calculations that include more of the molecular environment yield shorter times. The adaptive-mutation experiments themselves have alternative classical explanations in many cases. The idea remains a possible mechanism for a disputed phenomenon. It is not an established modification of evolutionary theory.

McFadden and Al-Khalili later surveyed a wider set of quantum effects in biology: tunneling in enzymes, coherent energy transfer in photosynthesis, the radical-pair mechanism for magnetoreception, and a proposed vibration-assisted tunneling in olfaction. Some of these effects are measured. Their functional importance varies. The adaptive-mutation model is the most specific claim that quantum coherence could bias the generation of heritable variation. That claim is still open. The broader observation that quantum mechanics is part of the chemistry of life is not.

title: Quantum Biology and Evolution
paras: Evolution is a classical process at the scale of populations. Mutation, selection, drift, and recombination are described by ordinary population genetics. The underlying chemistry of mutation and catalysis includes quantum steps. Those steps do not change the structure of the evolutionary account. They change the rates and the channels through which variation appears.

Proton and electron tunneling contribute to mutation. A proton that tunnels across a hydrogen bond in a base pair can produce a tautomeric form that mispairs. The contribution is small compared with copying errors and chemical damage. It is measurable in some systems by isotope effects. Electron tunneling occurs in the active sites of some repair enzymes. The proteins have evolved to position the reactants so that the tunneling rate is useful. The positioning is classical. The transfer step is quantum. Selection acts on the outcome, not on the mechanism.

Photosynthetic energy transfer and enzyme catalysis show coherent or tunneling contributions under physiological conditions. These processes affect the efficiency with which organisms capture energy and carry out metabolism. Efficiency is a selectable trait. Organisms that harness the quantum step more effectively leave more offspring, other things equal. The quantum step itself is not selected. The molecular architecture that makes the step available is selected. The distinction matters. Evolution does not need to “know” about quantum mechanics. It needs only to retain variants that work.

No established mechanism allows a cell to maintain a macroscopic superposition of genetic states and to collapse that superposition preferentially toward adaptive outcomes. The adaptive-mutation model remains a proposal. Decoherence in the cellular environment is rapid. The successful description of the origin and spread of adaptations continues to be the classical one: variation arises, most of it is neutral or deleterious, a fraction is advantageous, and selection increases the frequency of the advantageous fraction. Quantum mechanics is part of the physics that generates the variation and powers the metabolism. It is not a separate evolutionary force.

The practical consequence is modest and real. Calculations of mutation rates, of catalytic rates, and of energy-transfer efficiency are more accurate when the quantum channels are included. The evolutionary conclusions drawn from those rates do not change. The tree of life, the genetic code, and the history of adaptations remain the same. Quantum biology refines the chemistry. It does not rewrite the theory of evolution.

title: Optics and Quantum Mechanics
paras: Classical optics treats light as a wave. Interference, diffraction, and polarization follow from the wave equation. The speed in vacuum is \( c \). In a medium it is \( c/n \), where \( n \) is the refractive index. Lenses and mirrors redirect rays according to the law of reflection and Snell’s law of refraction. These rules are exact in the geometric-optics limit and are recovered as the short-wavelength limit of the wave theory.

Quantum mechanics assigns an amplitude to each path a photon can take. The probability is the square of the sum of the amplitudes. The same rule produces the interference pattern in a double-slit experiment when single photons are sent one at a time. The photon is detected at one place. The pattern builds from many detections. No trajectory is observed between source and detector. The calculation uses every path.

The photoelectric effect and Compton scattering show that light delivers energy and momentum in discrete quanta. The energy of a photon is \( E = h\nu \). The momentum is \( E/c \). These relations are confirmed by the threshold frequencies of photoemission and by the wavelength shift in Compton scattering. The wave and particle descriptions are complementary. Each is exact in its domain. Neither is complete alone.

Quantum electrodynamics unifies the two. The electromagnetic field is quantized. Photons are its quanta. Electrons interact by exchanging virtual photons. The theory reproduces classical optics in the appropriate limit and adds the quantum corrections measured in the Lamb shift and the anomalous magnetic moment. Optics is the classical limit of quantum electrodynamics. The underlying rules are quantum.

title: Quantum Foam
paras: Wheeler suggested that spacetime at the Planck scale is not smooth. Geometry fluctuates. The fluctuations are large enough that the classical manifold description fails. He called the fluctuating geometry quantum foam. Virtual black holes, wormholes, and changes of topology appear and disappear on timescales of the Planck time. The average geometry over larger scales remains the smooth spacetime of general relativity.

No direct observation of the foam exists. Particle accelerators reach energies many orders of magnitude below the Planck energy. Indirect limits come from the absence of certain effects that large fluctuations would produce: dispersion of light from distant sources, or violations of Lorentz invariance. The limits constrain the size of the fluctuations but do not rule out a foamy structure at the Planck length.

The idea is a qualitative expectation from combining general relativity and quantum mechanics. A full quantum theory of gravity would replace the expectation with a definite spectrum of fluctuations or with a different microstructure. Until that theory exists, quantum foam remains a plausible picture of the short-distance regime and an untested one.

title: Decoherence
paras: A quantum system that interacts with its environment becomes entangled with the environment. The reduced state of the system, obtained by tracing over the environmental degrees of freedom, loses the off-diagonal terms that encode interference. The process is decoherence. It occurs rapidly for macroscopic objects. A dust grain in air decoheres in a time far shorter than any practical observation. Interference between macroscopically distinct positions becomes unobservable.

Decoherence does not destroy the global superposition. The full state of system plus environment remains pure if it began pure. The local description of the system alone becomes mixed. Interference terms are still present in the global state. They are dispersed into correlations with the environment and cannot be recovered without measuring the environment in a precisely controlled way. For ordinary environments that control is impossible.

The process explains why macroscopic superpositions are not seen. It does not by itself select one outcome. The global state still contains every branch. Decoherence makes the branches effectively independent. It supplies the physical reason that the measurement problem is invisible in practice. It does not solve the problem of why one branch is experienced. That question remains interpretation-dependent.

Decoherence rates have been calculated and measured for systems ranging from single ions to superconducting circuits. The agreement is quantitative. The phenomenon is established. Its implications for the ontology of quantum mechanics are not.

title: Quantum Mechanics of the Atom
paras: The electrons in an atom are described by the Schrödinger equation. The solutions are stationary states labelled by quantum numbers. The energy levels of hydrogen are \( E_n = -13.6\,\mathrm{eV}/n^2 \). Transitions between levels emit or absorb photons whose frequencies match the observed spectral lines.

The Pauli exclusion principle requires that no two electrons occupy the same state. The principle, together with the Coulomb interaction, produces the shell structure of the periodic table. Chemical bonding arises when atoms share or transfer electrons so as to fill or empty outer shells.

The uncertainty principle limits the simultaneous knowledge of position and momentum. An electron confined to an atomic volume must possess a minimum kinetic energy. That kinetic energy balances the electrostatic attraction and sets the size of the atom. The same balance determines the sizes of molecules and the lattice spacings of solids.

Measurement collapses the wave function onto an eigenstate of the measured observable. The probability of each outcome is the squared modulus of the corresponding amplitude. The rule has been confirmed in every tested system. The interpretation of the collapse remains open. The predictive content does not.

title: The Measurement of Time
paras: Time is measured by counting periodic processes. The rotation of the Earth, the orbit of the Moon, and the vibration of a quartz crystal have all served as clocks. The present definition of the second is 9 192 631 770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between two hyperfine levels of the caesium-133 atom.

Atomic clocks achieve stabilities better than one part in \( 10^{16} \). Optical clocks that use transitions in the visible or ultraviolet are expected to reach one part in \( 10^{18} \). At that level the gravitational redshift produced by a height difference of one centimetre becomes measurable. Clocks therefore function as gravimeters.

The same atomic transitions define the metre through the fixed value of the speed of light. Length and time are no longer independent. The practical realization of both units rests on the same quantum standard. The historical separation of the two quantities has been replaced by a single metrological foundation.

title: Worked Examples: Quantum Measurement
paras: Example 1. A spin-1/2 particle is prepared in the state \( (|\uparrow\rangle + |\downarrow\rangle)/\sqrt{2} \). What are the probabilities of measuring spin up or spin down along the z-axis?
Each probability is \( |1/\sqrt{2}|^2 = 1/2 \).
Example 2. The same particle is measured and found to be up. It is then measured again immediately along the same axis. What is the outcome?
The second measurement yields up with certainty. The state has collapsed to \( |\uparrow\rangle \).
Example 3. An electron is confined to a one-dimensional box of width 0.1 nm. What is the minimum uncertainty in its momentum? What kinetic energy does that imply?

\( \Delta x \approx 0.1 \) nm. \( \Delta p \ge \hbar/(2\Delta x) \approx 5 \times 10^{-25} \) kg m s\(^{-1}\). \( E \ge (\Delta p)^2/(2m) \approx 1 \) eV. The estimate matches the order of magnitude of atomic energy levels.
Example 4. A radioactive nucleus has a half-life of 1 hour. What is the probability that it decays in the next minute?
Decay constant \( \lambda = \ln 2 / T_{1/2} \). Probability in time \( t \ll T_{1/2} \) is \( \approx \lambda t = 0.0115 \).
The calculations illustrate the Born rule, state reduction, the uncertainty principle and exponential decay—the operational content of quantum measurement.

title: Worked Examples: Quantum Entanglement
paras: Example 1. The singlet state of two spin-1/2 particles is \[ |\psi\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(|\uparrow\downarrow\rangle - |\downarrow\uparrow\rangle\bigr). \] What is the probability that both particles give the same result when measured along the same axis?
The probability is zero. The outcomes are perfectly anti-correlated.
Example 2. The same state is measured with the two analysers at a relative angle \(\theta\). What is the probability that the outcomes differ?

The probability is \(\cos^2(\theta/2)\). For \(\theta = 0\) the probability is 1 (always different). For \(\theta = 120^\circ\) the probability is 1/4. The result violates the Bell inequality that any local hidden-variable theory must satisfy.

Example 3. An entangled photon pair is produced in the state \[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(|HH\rangle + |VV\rangle\bigr). \] One photon is measured in the diagonal basis and found to be \(D\). What is the state of the other photon?
The other photon is immediately in the state \(D\). The measurement has projected the joint state.
Example 4. Two parties share a singlet. Alice measures her spin along \(z\) and obtains \(\uparrow\). She tells Bob the result by ordinary communication. What can Bob conclude about his own spin?

Bob knows his spin is \(\downarrow\) along \(z\). He cannot use the information to send a signal faster than light, because Alice’s outcome is random. The correlations appear only after the results are compared.

These examples recover the perfect anti-correlations, the angular dependence that violates Bell inequalities, the instantaneous update of the joint state, and the no-communication theorem—the operational content of entanglement.

title: Bell’s Theorem
paras: Bell’s theorem demonstrates that the statistical predictions of quantum mechanics for entangled particles cannot be reproduced by any local hidden-variable theory.

Two particles are prepared in an entangled state and sent to distant observers. Each observer chooses a measurement setting and records a binary outcome. A local hidden-variable theory assumes that the outcomes are predetermined by variables carried with the particles and that each observer’s result depends only on the local setting and on those shared variables. Under this assumption the correlations obey an inequality. One standard form (CHSH) states that a certain combination of four correlation functions cannot exceed 2 in absolute value.

Quantum mechanics predicts a larger value. For the spin singlet the correlation is minus the cosine of the angle between the analysers. Suitable choices of angle yield \( 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828 \). The quantum prediction therefore lies outside the bound required by local hidden variables.

Experiments with entangled photons, ions and superconducting circuits have measured the quantum value and violated the inequality. The violations persist when the measurement settings are chosen after the particles have left the source, closing the locality loophole, and when detection efficiencies are high enough to close the detection loophole. The observed correlations cannot be explained by any assignment of predetermined local properties.

The theorem does not imply that signals can be sent faster than light. Quantum mechanics itself forbids controllable signalling. It shows only that the correlations are stronger than those permitted by local pre-existing values. The experimental confirmation of that stronger correlation is one of the sharpest results in the foundations of physics.

title: Quantum Computing
paras: A quantum computer stores information in qubits. A qubit is a two-level quantum system that can exist in a superposition of its basis states. An \( n \)-qubit register can therefore occupy a superposition of all \( 2^n \) classical bit strings simultaneously.

Entanglement and interference allow certain algorithms to extract global properties of a function with fewer queries than any classical algorithm. Shor’s algorithm factors large integers in polynomial time by finding the period of a modular exponential function. Grover’s algorithm searches an unstructured database of \( N \) items in roughly \( \sqrt{N} \) steps. Both rely on the coherent evolution of superpositions and on a final measurement that yields the desired result with high probability.

The practical obstacles are decoherence and gate errors. Interaction with the environment destroys the relative phases that encode the computation. Quantum error-correcting codes spread the logical information across many physical qubits so that local errors can be detected and reversed without measuring the logical state. Fault-tolerant thresholds exist: if the physical error rate lies below a few parts in \( 10^3 \) to \( 10^4 \), arbitrarily long computations are possible in principle.

Present devices contain tens to a few hundred qubits and execute circuits of limited depth. They have demonstrated small instances of quantum advantage on specially chosen sampling tasks. They have not yet run Shor’s algorithm on integers large enough to threaten cryptographic systems. The gap between the theoretical algorithms and large-scale, error-corrected machines remains the central engineering problem.

The computational model does not violate the Church–Turing thesis in its modern form. It supplies a different complexity scaling for particular problems. The scaling originates in the same interference of amplitudes that appears in every other quantum experiment.

title: Quantum Gravity
paras: Quantum gravity is the attempt to reconcile general relativity with quantum mechanics. General relativity describes spacetime as a dynamical geometry whose curvature is fixed by the distribution of energy and momentum. Quantum mechanics describes matter and fields by operators on a Hilbert space and by amplitudes that interfere. At ordinary energies the two frameworks are used in succession: quantum fields propagate on a fixed classical background. The approximation fails when curvature radii approach the Planck length, approximately \( 10^{-35} \) m, or when energies approach the Planck energy, approximately \( 10^{19} \) GeV.

No complete theory is known. Several research programmes exist. String theory replaces point particles by extended objects whose vibrational modes include a massless spin-2 state that couples as a graviton. Consistent quantisation requires additional spatial dimensions and supersymmetry. The theory is perturbatively finite at each order and contains general relativity as a low-energy limit. It has not yet produced a unique four-dimensional vacuum that reproduces the observed particle spectrum and cosmological constant.

Loop quantum gravity quantises the geometry itself. Areas and volumes become discrete operators. The classical singularity of a black hole or of the cosmological big bang is replaced by a bounce in some models. The recovery of a smooth spacetime at large scales and the incorporation of the Standard Model remain open.

Other approaches—asymptotic safety, causal dynamical triangulations, and emergent-gravity scenarios—explore different quantisation schemes or different ontological starting points. None has been experimentally confirmed. The only present evidence that a quantum theory of gravity is required is the existence of singularities in the classical theory and the expectation that quantum effects cannot be neglected at the Planck scale.

The problem is therefore well-posed and unsolved. Its solution will determine whether spacetime is fundamental or emergent, whether information is preserved in black-hole evaporation, and whether the initial conditions of the universe can be derived rather than postulated.

title: Loop Quantum Gravity
paras: Loop quantum gravity is a non-perturbative, background-independent quantisation of general relativity. The fundamental variables are holonomies of the Ashtekar connection along paths and fluxes of the densitised triad through surfaces. These variables are promoted to operators on a Hilbert space of spin-network states. A spin network is a graph whose edges carry SU(2) representations and whose nodes carry invariant tensors.

The area of a surface and the volume of a region become discrete operators. Their spectra are bounded below by multiples of the Planck area and the Planck volume. The classical continuum geometry is recovered only as an approximation when the spin network is finely grained and the expectation values of the geometric operators are large compared with the Planck scale.

The dynamics are encoded in a Hamiltonian constraint. Solutions of the constraint define the physical Hilbert space. In cosmological models the same techniques yield a difference equation for the scale factor. The equation replaces the big-bang singularity by a bounce at a critical density of order the Planck density. The bounce connects a contracting phase to an expanding phase. Whether the bounce is generic in the full theory is not yet established.

Matter can be coupled. Fermions and gauge fields are incorporated by extending the spin-network labels. The recovery of the Standard Model spectrum and of a realistic value of the cosmological constant has not been achieved. The theory also lacks a complete demonstration that its low-energy limit is classical general relativity plus quantum field theory on curved spacetime, although several calculations of graviton propagators and of black-hole entropy are consistent with that limit.

Loop quantum gravity therefore supplies a concrete realisation of discrete quantum geometry and a possible resolution of cosmological singularities. It remains incomplete as a unified theory of all interactions and as a fully controlled continuum limit.

title: Quantum Field Theory
paras: Quantum field theory is the framework that combines quantum mechanics with special relativity. The fundamental objects are fields defined at every point of spacetime. Particles appear as quanta of those fields. The theory is formulated so that the laws take the same form in every inertial frame and so that no signal propagates faster than light.

Interactions are local. The Lagrangian density at each point depends only on the fields and their derivatives at that point. The resulting S-matrix elements are computed by Feynman diagrams. Each diagram corresponds to a possible sequence of emissions and absorptions. The sum of diagrams yields the probability amplitude for a given process. Renormalisation absorbs the infinite contributions of high-energy virtual particles into a finite number of measured parameters. After renormalisation the predictions are finite and accurate.

The Standard Model is a quantum field theory. Its gauge symmetries dictate the interactions of quarks, leptons and the Higgs field. Quantum electrodynamics, the oldest and simplest part, predicts the anomalous magnetic moment of the electron to more than ten significant figures. Quantum chromodynamics accounts for the spectrum and scattering of hadrons once confinement is accepted. The electroweak theory unifies the electromagnetic and weak interactions and predicted the W, Z and Higgs bosons before they were observed.

The framework fails when gravity becomes strong. No consistent quantum field theory of the metric itself is known. At accessible energies, however, quantum field theory is the most precise description of nature that exists. Every confirmed particle-physics experiment is a test of it.

title: Quantum Optics
paras: Quantum optics studies the quantum properties of light and its interaction with matter at the level of individual photons and atoms. A single-photon source emits one photon at a time. A single-photon detector registers that photon with high efficiency. Interference of single photons in a Mach–Zehnder interferometer demonstrates that the photon takes both paths when no which-path information is available.

Cavity quantum electrodynamics couples an atom to a high-finesse optical cavity. The coupling strength can exceed the decay rates, producing reversible exchange of excitation—vacuum Rabi oscillations. The same regime allows deterministic generation of entangled atom–photon states and the realisation of quantum gates between distant atoms mediated by photons.

Squeezed light has reduced noise in one quadrature at the expense of increased noise in the conjugate quadrature. It improves the sensitivity of interferometers beyond the standard quantum limit and is used in gravitational-wave detectors. Photon antibunching, Hong–Ou–Mandel interference and Bell tests with photons are routine. Quantum optics supplies both the experimental foundation of quantum information and a precision tool for metrology.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Non-Locality
paras: Quantum entanglement is a correlation between subsystems that cannot be reproduced by any assignment of pre-existing local properties. For two spin-1/2 particles in the singlet state the outcomes of spin measurements along the same axis are perfectly anti-correlated. Along different axes the correlation is \( -\cos\theta \).

Bell inequalities bound the correlations permitted by local hidden-variable theories. Quantum mechanics exceeds those bounds. Experiments with photons, atoms and superconducting circuits have violated the inequalities under conditions that close the principal loopholes. The violations demonstrate that nature does not admit a local realist description of the sort assumed by the inequalities.

Entanglement does not permit faster-than-light signalling. The marginal statistics for each party remain random. Only the joint statistics reveal the correlation. The same resource powers quantum teleportation, super-dense coding and device-independent cryptography. Entanglement is therefore both a foundational feature of quantum mechanics and a practical resource for information processing.

title: Quantum Electrodynamics
paras: Quantum electrodynamics is the quantum field theory of the electromagnetic interaction. It describes electrons, positrons and photons. The interaction is local and gauge-invariant. The coupling constant is the fine-structure constant \( \alpha \approx 1/137 \).

Feynman diagrams organise the perturbative expansion. Each vertex contributes a factor of the coupling. Internal lines represent virtual particles. The sum of diagrams at a given order yields the amplitude for a process. Renormalisation absorbs the divergences into the measured values of the electron mass and charge. After renormalisation every prediction is finite.

The theory is the most precise in physics. The anomalous magnetic moment of the electron agrees with experiment to more than ten significant figures. The Lamb shift, the hyperfine structure of hydrogen and the scattering of electrons and positrons are likewise predicted to high accuracy. Quantum electrodynamics is the unbroken \( U(1) \) sector of the Standard Model. It is the prototype of a successful quantum field theory.

title: Further Aspects of Quantum Biology
paras: Quantum effects in biology are real but limited. Electron tunnelling occurs in photosynthetic reaction centres and in some enzymes. Proton tunnelling contributes to certain hydrogen-transfer reactions. Coherent energy transfer has been observed in photosynthetic complexes at low temperature. Whether the coherence survives long enough to improve efficiency at physiological temperature remains debated.

The claims for quantum computation in the brain or for quantum-enhanced olfaction lack experimental support. The thermal environment of a cell destroys coherence on timescales far shorter than those required for such processes. Ordinary quantum chemistry—tunnelling, zero-point energy, discrete spectra—is sufficient to explain the established cases. Exotic macroscopic quantum effects are not required.

The field therefore consists of a small set of confirmed tunnelling and coherence phenomena embedded in an otherwise classical biochemical framework. The confirmed cases are interesting. They do not rewrite the foundations of biology.

title: Further Aspects of Quantum Effects in Genetics
paras: Mutations are changes in nucleotide sequence. Some arise from quantum tunnelling of protons in DNA base pairs. The tunnelling can produce tautomeric forms that pair incorrectly during replication. The rate is low. It is nevertheless a calculated contribution to the spontaneous mutation rate.

The contribution does not imply that evolution is directed by quantum mechanics. Tunnelling supplies one source of random variation among others—thermal fluctuations, chemical damage, replication errors. Selection acts on the phenotypic consequences regardless of the physical origin of the mutation. No evidence indicates that organisms control the tunnelling rate to produce adaptive mutations.
The established quantum contribution is therefore limited to a fraction of spontaneous point mutations. It is real. It does not alter the neo-Darwinian account of variation and selection.

title: Further Aspects of Quantum Foam
paras: Quantum foam is the expected structure of spacetime at the Planck scale. The uncertainty principle applied to the metric implies fluctuations in geometry whose amplitude becomes order-one at lengths of \( 10^{-35} \) m. The fluctuations are not a classical foam that can be pictured. They are quantum fluctuations of the gravitational field.

No experiment has resolved the Planck length. Indirect bounds from Lorentz invariance and from the absence of anomalous dispersion in high-energy photons constrain the size of certain foam-induced effects. The constraints are many orders of magnitude above the Planck scale. They do not rule out foam. They rule out large, observable violations of Lorentz symmetry produced by it.

The concept remains a qualitative expectation of any quantum theory of gravity. It has not been derived from a completed theory. It serves as a reminder that classical spacetime is an approximation expected to fail at sufficiently short distances.

title: Further Aspects of Quantum Entanglement
paras: Entanglement is monogamous. A system maximally entangled with one partner cannot be entangled with a third. The monogamy relation is quantitative. It bounds the sum of the squared concurrences. The bound is saturated by the singlet and by GHZ states in appropriate limits.

Entanglement can be distilled. From many weakly entangled pairs one can extract a smaller number of nearly maximally entangled pairs by local operations and classical communication. The reverse process—entanglement dilution—converts maximally entangled pairs into a larger number of weakly entangled pairs. The two processes define the entanglement of formation and the distillable entanglement. For pure bipartite states the two measures coincide. For mixed states they may differ. The difference is a signature of bound entanglement that cannot be distilled.

title: Further Aspects of Quantum Optics
paras: The Hong–Ou–Mandel effect is the interference of two identical photons at a beam splitter. When the photons arrive simultaneously they exit together in the same output port. The coincidence rate drops to zero. The dip is a direct signature of bosonic exchange symmetry. It is used to characterise single-photon sources and to implement linear-optical quantum gates.

Cavity QED in the strong-coupling regime produces vacuum Rabi splitting. The atom and the cavity mode exchange a single excitation coherently. The splitting is resolved when the coupling exceeds the decay rates. The same regime enables the deterministic generation of atom–photon entanglement and the realisation of photon-mediated gates between distant atoms. Both the Hong–Ou–Mandel dip and the vacuum Rabi splitting are routine laboratory observations. They confirm the particle nature of light and the coherent interaction of single quanta.

title: Quantum Error Correction
paras: Quantum error correction protects quantum information against decoherence and gate errors. A logical qubit is encoded in a subspace of several physical qubits. The code detects errors by measuring stabiliser operators that commute with the logical operators. The measurement reveals the error without revealing the logical state. A recovery operation then restores the state.

The surface code is a leading candidate. It requires only nearest-neighbour interactions on a two-dimensional lattice. Its threshold is approximately 1 percent. Below the threshold, increasing the code distance suppresses the logical error rate exponentially. Above the threshold, adding qubits makes the error worse. Present devices operate near or below the threshold for small distances. Scaling to the distances required for useful algorithms remains an engineering challenge. The existence of the threshold shows that fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in principle.

title: Further Aspects of Quantum Error Correction
paras: The threshold theorem states that if the physical error rate lies below a constant threshold, then arbitrarily long quantum computations can be performed with only polylogarithmic overhead. The theorem requires that errors are local and that fresh ancilla qubits can be supplied. It does not require that the errors are independent, only that their correlations decay sufficiently fast.

Magic-state distillation converts noisy non-Clifford states into purer ones. It is the leading method for implementing the non-Clifford gates required for universality. The overhead is large. Reducing it is an active research area. Concatenated codes and topological codes both achieve thresholds. Topological codes are preferred for their higher thresholds and for their compatibility with two-dimensional architectures. The theorem guarantees that fault tolerance is possible. It does not guarantee that it is easy.

title: Anomalies in Quantum Field Theory
paras: Anomalies are symmetries of the classical action that are broken by quantum effects. The chiral anomaly is the non-conservation of the axial current in the presence of gauge fields. It is required for the decay of the neutral pion and for the resolution of the U(1) problem in QCD. Gauge anomalies must cancel for consistency. In the Standard Model they cancel between quarks and leptons.

The cancellation is a constraint on the particle content. It is satisfied by the observed fermions. Gravitational anomalies impose further constraints. Anomalies are not defects. They are calculable quantum effects that have observable consequences. Their cancellation or non-cancellation determines which theories are consistent.

title: Holography and Entanglement
paras: The Ryu–Takayanagi formula equates the entanglement entropy of a boundary region with the area of a bulk minimal surface. The formula has been verified in many examples. It suggests that spacetime geometry is encoded in the entanglement structure of the boundary theory. The suggestion is precise in anti-de Sitter space. Its extension to other asymptotics is incomplete.

Entanglement wedge reconstruction shows that bulk operators inside the wedge can be represented as boundary operators. The reconstruction is state-dependent for operators behind horizons. The dependence is consistent with the island calculations of black-hole evaporation. Holography therefore supplies both a definition of quantum gravity in certain spacetimes and a concrete realisation of the idea that geometry emerges from entanglement.

title: Quantum Extremal Surfaces
paras: A quantum extremal surface is a surface that extremises the generalised entropy. It reduces to the ordinary Ryu–Takayanagi surface when the bulk entropy is negligible. When the bulk entropy is large the surface moves. In the island calculation the quantum extremal surface lies inside the horizon after the Page time. Its area plus the bulk entropy of the island and the radiation gives the Page curve.

The surface is a generalisation of the classical extremal surface. It incorporates the leading quantum correction. Higher-order corrections exist. They are small in the semi-classical limit. The concept unifies the classical area term with the bulk entanglement. It is the geometric object that appears in the island formula and in the derivation of the Page curve.

title: The Measurement Problem
paras: The measurement problem is the question of how a definite outcome emerges from a quantum superposition. The Schrödinger equation is linear and deterministic. It does not by itself select one outcome. The Born rule gives probabilities. It does not describe the occurrence of a single result. Collapse postulates add the selection by hand. They are not derived from the unitary dynamics.

Decoherence explains the suppression of interference. It does not explain the occurrence of one outcome rather than another. Many-worlds interpretations deny that a selection occurs. Bohmian mechanics adds particle positions. Objective-collapse models modify the equation. None is established. The problem is the gap between the unitary formalism and the definite events of experience. The gap remains open.

title: Decoherence in Detail
paras: Decoherence is the loss of phase coherence between components of a superposition through interaction with an environment. The reduced density matrix of the system becomes diagonal in a preferred basis. Interference terms vanish. The preferred basis is selected by the interaction Hamiltonian. For macroscopic objects the basis is approximately the position basis.

The process is rapid for macroscopic superpositions. It is slow for carefully isolated microscopic systems. Decoherence accounts for the classical appearance of everyday objects. It does not solve the measurement problem. The diagonal density matrix is an improper mixture. It does not correspond to a definite outcome. The process is necessary for classicality. It is not sufficient for the emergence of single events.

title: Quantum Darwinism
paras: Quantum Darwinism proposes that the classical world emerges through the redundant encoding of information in the environment. Pointer states are those that survive decoherence and proliferate their information. Observers who access fragments of the environment obtain the same information. The redundancy defines objectivity.

The proposal accounts for the preferred basis and for the agreement among observers. It does not select a single outcome. All pointer states are encoded. The appearance of a single outcome still requires an interpretation of the branching or an additional postulate. The framework is consistent with decoherence. It extends it by emphasising redundancy. It remains an account of classicality, not a solution to the measurement problem.

title: Relational Quantum Mechanics
paras: Relational quantum mechanics asserts that the quantum state of a system is relative to another system. There is no absolute state. Events are interactions. The state is the information that one system has about another. The approach dissolves the measurement problem by denying the existence of an observer-independent state.

The approach is consistent with the predictions of quantum mechanics. It requires care in the treatment of sequences of measurements. It does not add dynamical postulates. Its cost is the abandonment of an absolute quantum state. The cost is accepted by its proponents as the price of consistency. The approach remains a minority interpretation.

title: Quantum Bayesianism
paras: Quantum Bayesianism interprets the quantum state as an agent’s information or degrees of belief. The state is not a property of the system. It is a property of the agent. Measurement updates the agent’s beliefs. The approach avoids ontological questions about collapse. It relocates the state to the agent.

The approach reproduces the operational predictions. It must explain why agents who communicate agree. The explanation relies on the common information acquired through interaction. The approach is operationally clear. Its metaphysical claim—that the state is not ontic—is disputed. The dispute does not affect the calculations. It affects the interpretation of what the calculations describe.

title: The Quantum-to-Classical Transition
paras: The quantum-to-classical transition is the emergence of classical behaviour from quantum mechanics. Decoherence suppresses interference. The remaining diagonal density matrix can be interpreted as a classical mixture for practical purposes. The interpretation is adequate for prediction. It is incomplete for ontology.

The transition is continuous. Mesoscopic systems display partial coherence. The degree of classicality increases with the separation of the components and with the strength of the environmental interaction. No sharp boundary exists. The transition is well-described by decoherence for all practical purposes. The residual conceptual questions are those of the measurement problem. They are not resolved by the practical success.

title: Bell’s Theorem in Detail
paras: Bell’s theorem states that no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce the predictions of quantum mechanics. The CHSH inequality bounds the correlations permitted by local realism. Quantum mechanics predicts a violation up to \( 2\sqrt{2} \). Experiments have measured violations close to the quantum bound. The experiments have closed the detection, locality and freedom-of-choice loopholes.

The theorem does not require non-local signalling. It requires that the outcomes are not determined by local variables in the manner assumed by the inequality. The experimental violations confirm the quantum predictions. They exclude local realistic completions of the sort Bell considered. They do not exclude all conceivable completions. They exclude those that satisfy the assumptions of the theorem.

title: Quantum Steering
paras: Quantum steering is the ability of one party to influence the state of a distant party by choice of measurement. It is intermediate between entanglement and Bell non-locality. Not all entangled states are steerable. All Bell-nonlocal states are steerable. Steering can be verified with one trusted and one untrusted party.

The phenomenon has been demonstrated experimentally. It is a resource for one-sided device-independent cryptography. The hierarchy—entanglement, steering, Bell non-locality—organises the strengths of quantum correlation. Each level excludes a larger set of classical models. Steering is the intermediate level. It is both theoretically sharp and experimentally accessible.

title: Device-Independent Quantum Information
paras: Device-independent protocols rely only on the observed correlations. They do not require characterisation of the devices. Security is certified by the violation of a Bell inequality. The certification is independent of the internal workings of the apparatus. Quantum key distribution and random-number generation have been implemented in the device-independent setting.

The implementations require high-efficiency detection and space-like separation. Both have been achieved. The rates are low. The principle is established. Practical deployment awaits higher rates and longer distances. The approach eliminates side-channel attacks that exploit imperfect device characterisation. It replaces them with the requirement of a loophole-free Bell violation.

title: Quantum Key Distribution
paras: Quantum key distribution allows two parties to generate a shared secret key. Security rests on the no-cloning theorem and on the disturbance caused by measurement. The BB84 protocol uses four polarisation states. The E91 protocol uses entangled pairs and Bell violation. Both have been implemented over optical fibre and free space.

The secret-key rate decreases with distance because of loss and noise. Quantum repeaters are required for global distances. Prototype repeaters exist. They are not yet practical. The security proofs assume ideal devices or are device-independent. Real devices introduce side channels. Countermeasures exist. The protocols are information-theoretically secure under the stated assumptions. The assumptions must be enforced in practice.

title: Quantum Teleportation
paras: Quantum teleportation transfers an unknown quantum state from one system to another using a shared entangled pair and classical communication. The sender performs a joint measurement. The receiver applies a correction conditioned on the classical result. The state is destroyed at the sender and recreated at the receiver. No information is transmitted faster than light.

Teleportation has been demonstrated with photons, atoms, ions and superconducting circuits. It is a primitive for quantum networks and for measurement-based computation. The fidelity is limited by the quality of the entanglement and by the accuracy of the operations. High-fidelity teleportation over laboratory distances is routine. Extension to long distances requires quantum repeaters. The protocol is both a fundamental demonstration and a practical tool.

title: Quantum Networks
paras: A quantum network distributes entanglement and transmits quantum states among multiple nodes. The nodes are quantum processors or memories. The links are photonic channels. Quantum repeaters extend the range by entanglement swapping and purification. The network enables distributed quantum computation, blind quantum computation and long-distance key distribution.

Prototype networks with a few nodes exist. They demonstrate entanglement distribution and teleportation. Scaling to many nodes requires memories with long coherence times, high-efficiency interfaces, and error correction. The requirements are engineering challenges. The architectural principles are established. The network is the quantum analogue of the classical internet. It does not yet exist at comparable scale.

title: Blind Quantum Computation
paras: Blind quantum computation allows a client to delegate a computation to a server without revealing the input, the output or the algorithm. The client prepares single qubits and sends them to the server. The server entangles them and measures according to instructions. The instructions are chosen so that the server learns nothing about the computation. The client obtains the result.

The protocol has been demonstrated with photonic systems. Security rests on the no-signalling principle and on the client’s ability to prepare states from a restricted set. The protocol enables private computation on a remote quantum computer. It does not require the client to possess a universal quantum computer. The client needs only to prepare and measure single qubits. The capability is a distinctive feature of quantum networks.

title: Topological Quantum Computation
paras: Topological quantum computation encodes information in non-Abelian anyons. The information is stored in the fusion space. Gates are implemented by braiding. The braiding is topological. It is insensitive to local perturbations. The protection is passive. Error correction is still required for non-topological operations and for leakage.

Ising anyons are realised in the fractional quantum Hall state at filling factor 5/2 and in certain superconducting systems. They are not universal. Additional non-topological gates are needed. Fibonacci anyons are universal. They have not been realised. The approach offers high thresholds in principle. The experimental realisation of non-Abelian anyons with the required properties remains incomplete. The theoretical framework is mature.

title: Measurement-Based Quantum Computation
paras: Measurement-based quantum computation performs the computation by a sequence of single-qubit measurements on a pre-entangled resource state. The resource is a cluster state or a graph state. The measurements are adaptive. The basis of each measurement depends on previous outcomes. The computation is equivalent to the circuit model.

The approach separates the creation of entanglement from the computation. The entanglement can be prepared offline. The computation itself consists of measurements. The separation is advantageous for photonic implementations. Photon loss remains the principal error. Error correction is possible. The model is universal. It has been demonstrated on small scales. Scaling requires high-fidelity resource states and feed-forward.

title: Adiabatic Quantum Computation
paras: Adiabatic quantum computation encodes the solution of a problem in the ground state of a final Hamiltonian. The system is prepared in the ground state of an initial Hamiltonian and evolved slowly to the final Hamiltonian. The adiabatic theorem guarantees that the system remains in the ground state if the evolution is slow enough. The runtime scales with the inverse square of the minimum gap.

The model is universal. It is equivalent to the circuit model. Practical implementations are limited by the gap and by thermal excitations. Quantum annealing is a related heuristic. It does not guarantee the ground state. Both approaches are studied for optimisation problems. Speed-ups over classical algorithms are not guaranteed for all instances. They are possible for some.

title: Quantum Annealing
paras: Quantum annealing is a heuristic method for finding the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian. A transverse field is applied and slowly reduced. Tunnelling allows the system to escape local minima. The method does not guarantee the optimal solution. It can outperform simulated annealing on some instances. It can underperform on others.

Commercial devices implement quantum annealing with thousands of qubits. The qubits are noisy. The connectivity is limited. Benchmarking against classical algorithms is ongoing. Advantages have been claimed for specific problem classes. The claims are contested. The devices are useful for studying quantum dynamics. Their advantage for practical optimisation remains unproven.

title: Variational Quantum Algorithms
paras: Variational quantum algorithms use a parameterised quantum circuit and a classical optimiser. The circuit prepares a trial state. The classical optimiser adjusts the parameters to minimise a cost function. The approach is hybrid. It is suitable for noisy intermediate-scale devices. The quantum approximate optimisation algorithm and the variational quantum eigensolver are examples.

The algorithms do not require fault tolerance. Their performance is limited by noise and by the difficulty of the classical optimisation. Barren plateaus—regions of exponentially small gradients—impede training for some circuits. Mitigation strategies exist. The algorithms are a practical approach for present hardware. Their asymptotic advantage is not established.

title: Substantial Expansion: Quantum Field Theory
paras: Quantum field theory is the framework that combines quantum mechanics with special relativity. Particles are excitations of fields. Interactions are local. The S-matrix is computed perturbatively by Feynman diagrams or non-perturbatively by lattice methods or by other techniques. Renormalisation renders the predictions finite in renormalisable theories.

The framework encompasses the Standard Model, effective theories of the strong interaction, and condensed-matter systems. It predicts the existence of antiparticles, the spin-statistics connection, and the CPT theorem. It does not include gravity in a consistent way. Attempts to quantise gravity perturbatively fail because the theory is non-renormalisable. Non-perturbative approaches—string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety—remain incomplete. Quantum field theory is nevertheless the language in which the most precise predictions in physics are formulated.

title: Dark Matter
paras: Galaxies rotate faster in their outer regions than the visible mass can explain. Clusters of galaxies bend light and bind hot gas more strongly than their luminous matter allows. The cosmic microwave background shows acoustic peaks whose positions require additional non-baryonic matter. These observations converge on a component that gravitates but does not emit, absorb, or scatter light at detectable levels. It is called dark matter.

The density of dark matter is about five times the density of ordinary matter. It is cold, meaning that its particles moved slowly when structures formed. Cold dark matter collapses into halos. Ordinary matter falls into the halos and forms galaxies. The halos are larger than the visible galaxies. Their presence is inferred from rotation curves, gravitational lensing, and the growth of structure.

No dark-matter particle has been detected in the laboratory. Candidates include weakly interacting massive particles, axions, and sterile neutrinos. Direct-detection experiments set limits on the scattering cross-section. Indirect searches look for annihilation products. Collider searches look for missing energy. None has produced a confirmed signal. The gravitational evidence remains. The identity of the matter does not.

Modified-gravity theories attempt to explain the observations without new particles. They reproduce some galactic rotation curves. They have greater difficulty with clusters, with the microwave background, and with the separation of mass and light in merging clusters. The dark-matter hypothesis accounts for all of these with one additional component. It is the working description. It is not yet a completed identification.

title: Dark Energy
paras: The expansion of the universe is accelerating. Type Ia supernovae at high redshift are fainter than they would be in a decelerating universe. The microwave-background acoustic peaks and the large-scale distribution of galaxies independently require a component that drives acceleration. The component has negative pressure. Its energy density is roughly constant as the universe expands. It is called dark energy.

The simplest model is a cosmological constant. Einstein introduced the term to permit a static universe. It was later set to zero. The observations revive it with a small positive value. The constant corresponds to an energy density of about \( 10^{-29} \) grams per cubic centimeter. Quantum field theory predicts a far larger vacuum energy. The discrepancy is many orders of magnitude. No accepted resolution exists.

Other models allow the density to vary slowly. They are parameterized by an equation-of-state index \( w \). Current data are consistent with \( w = -1 \), the value for a cosmological constant, to within a few percent. Future surveys of supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, and weak lensing will tighten the constraint. A clear departure from \( -1 \) would rule out the simplest model.

Dark energy dominates the present energy budget. It did not dominate in the past. Its presence sets the ultimate fate of the expansion. If it remains constant, the expansion continues forever and galaxies beyond the local group eventually leave the observable universe. The inference rests on the measured acceleration and on the assumption that the component persists. Both are supported by present data. Both remain open to revision.

title: Dark Energy and the Accelerating Universe
paras: Distant Type Ia supernovae are fainter than expected in a decelerating universe. The microwave-background acoustic peaks and the baryon-acoustic-oscillation scale independently require a component that does not cluster and that has negative pressure. That component is dark energy. It constitutes approximately 70 percent of the present energy density.

The simplest model is a cosmological constant with equation-of-state parameter \( w = -1 \). More general models allow \( w \) to vary with time. Current data are consistent with a constant. The energy density of a true cosmological constant is unchanging. It therefore dominated only recently, when the matter density had fallen sufficiently. The transition to acceleration occurred at redshift \( z \approx 0.7 \).

The cosmological-constant problem is the discrepancy between the observed value and the far larger value expected from quantum-field zero-point energies. No accepted solution exists. Quintessence models replace the constant with a slowly rolling scalar field. Modified-gravity models alter the Einstein equation on large scales. All of these proposals remain viable because the only observational constraints are the expansion history and the growth rate of structure, both of which are still compatible with a pure cosmological constant.

title: Dark Matter and Dark Energy
paras: Dark matter and dark energy are the two dominant components of the present universe. Neither emits, absorbs nor scatters light. Both are detected solely through their gravitational effects.

Dark matter constitutes approximately 25 percent of the energy density. Galaxy rotation curves remain flat at radii where the visible mass is insufficient. Clusters of galaxies are likewise too massive for the light they emit. Gravitational lensing maps a mass distribution that extends far beyond the luminous component. On cosmological scales cold dark matter is required for structure to grow at the observed rate after recombination. The particles have not been identified. Candidates include weakly interacting massive particles, axions and primordial black holes. Laboratory searches continue.

Dark energy constitutes approximately 70 percent of the energy density. Type Ia supernovae at high redshift are fainter than expected in a matter-only universe. The acoustic scale of the microwave background and the baryon-acoustic-oscillation feature in galaxy surveys independently require a component with negative pressure. The simplest realisation is a cosmological constant with equation-of-state parameter \( w = -1 \). Current data are consistent with a constant. The energy density is many orders of magnitude smaller than the value expected from quantum-field zero-point energies. The discrepancy is the cosmological-constant problem.

Together the two components account for 95 percent of the present cosmic budget. Ordinary baryonic matter is the remaining 5 percent. The expansion history and the growth of structure are accurately described once both are included. Their microphysical nature remains unknown.

title: Dark Matter Detection
paras: Direct detection experiments search for the elastic scattering of dark-matter particles on nuclei or electrons. The expected rate is low. Detectors are placed underground to reduce cosmic-ray backgrounds. They use liquid xenon, liquid argon, or cryogenic crystals. No confirmed signal has been observed. The experiments exclude large regions of the parameter space for weakly interacting massive particles.

Indirect detection searches for annihilation or decay products—gamma rays, neutrinos, antimatter. Excesses have been reported and later attributed to astrophysical sources. Collider searches look for missing energy carried by particles that escape the detector. No significant excess has been confirmed. The absence of signals has pushed the favoured mass range upward and the favoured coupling strength downward. The particles, if they exist, have not yet been produced or detected in the laboratory.

title: Further Aspects of Dark Matter Detection
paras: Annual modulation is a predicted signature. The Earth’s orbital motion causes the dark-matter flux to vary by a few percent over the year. One experiment has reported a modulation. Others have not confirmed it. The discrepancy remains unresolved. Directional detectors aim to measure the arrival direction of the recoiling nucleus. The direction would point opposite the solar motion through the galactic halo. No directional detector has yet reached the required sensitivity.

Axion searches use resonant cavities in strong magnetic fields. The axion converts to a photon whose frequency equals the axion mass. The search is a scan in frequency. No signal has been found in the ranges examined. The remaining parameter space is large. Primordial black holes are constrained by microlensing, by dynamical effects on stars, and by the absence of evaporation signals. They can constitute at most a fraction of the dark matter in most mass windows. The experimental programme continues. The particles have not been identified.

title: The Cosmological Constant
paras: The cosmological constant is the energy density of the vacuum. It appears in the Einstein equation as a term proportional to the metric. Observations require a positive value whose density is approximately \( 6\times 10^{-10} \) J m\(^{-3}\). The value is constant in time in the simplest model. It dominates the present expansion.

Quantum field theory predicts a far larger value. The discrepancy is the cosmological-constant problem. No symmetry sets the constant to zero. Supersymmetry would cancel the leading contribution if unbroken. It is broken. Anthropic selection in a landscape of vacua can explain the smallness. It does not predict the value beyond the requirement that structure can form. The constant remains a measured parameter whose microscopic origin is unknown.

title: Oxidation and Reduction
paras: Oxidation is the loss of electrons. Reduction is the gain of electrons. The two processes occur together. The substance that loses electrons is oxidized. The substance that gains electrons is reduced. The pair constitutes a redox reaction.

The tendency of a half-reaction to occur is measured by its standard reduction potential. The potential is the voltage of a cell in which the half-reaction is coupled to the standard hydrogen electrode. A positive potential means the half-reaction proceeds spontaneously as a reduction under standard conditions. The difference in potential between two half-reactions gives the voltage of the corresponding galvanic cell and, through the relation \( \Delta G = -nFE \), the free-energy change.

The same scale organizes the chemistry of the elements. Metals with negative reduction potentials dissolve in acid. Metals with positive potentials do not. The potentials also determine the products of electrolysis and the feasibility of industrial redox processes. They remain the practical measure of electron-transfer tendency.

title: The Earth’s Atmosphere and Climate
paras: The atmosphere is a thin gaseous envelope whose composition is maintained by geological and biological fluxes. Nitrogen and oxygen dominate.
